meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with Romanic and Germanic influences, incorporating elements of statutory codification and customary practice)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended; Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLO, SR 955.01) of 10 November 2015, as amended; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 697j et seq.; Ordinance on the Beneficial Owner Registry (SR 221.434.3) of 27 November 2019, as amended; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis and 305ter.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts) duly notarized by a Swiss cantonal notary
Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent official registry excerpt from the country of origin of each non-Swiss corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chamber of Commerce, Companies Registry, or competent corporate registrar in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if origin is not a Hague signatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (passport copy certified by a competent authority) for each beneficial owner and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office, consulate, or notary in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address (e.g., utility bill or bank statement) for each beneficial owner, non-Swiss domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or municipal authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution confirming business relationship and source of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if applicable)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) for politically exposed persons (PEPs) pursuant to AMLA Art. 6 and FINMA Circular 2018/4. Screening must be performed against the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, Swiss autonomous sanctions adopting EU measures, and for cross-border banking activities, the US OFAC SDN list. Beneficial owners must be identified with a minimum threshold of 25% ownership or controlling interest. PEPs are subject to approval by senior management, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing monitoring for at least 12 months after ceasing PEP status. Additional scrutiny applies to transactions with high-risk jurisdictions listed by FATF or FINMA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Business Index (ZEFIX) – www.zefix.ch; Cantonal Commercial Registry (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce) e-counter via easiGov portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script and may be expressed in any of Switzerland's official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh). Names derived from a foreign language must be transliterated/transliterated into Latin characters and must not conflict with public policy, moral order, or the principle of truthfulness (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 950–951). The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must include a legal form suffix: 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Société Anonyme', 'SA', or equivalent. All name elements must be clearly readable and pronounceable in at least one official Swiss language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a formal written decision from the Cantonal Commercial Registry. An administrative appeal must be filed within 30 days of receipt of the rejection notice with the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht / Tribunal cantonal administratif) or the competent Data Protection and Commercial Registry supervisory authority. The appeal must state grounds and may request substitution of the proposed name. If the cantonal level confirms rejection, further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht / Tribunal administratif fédéral) in St. Gallen within 30 days. A rejected name may be modified and resubmitted at any time without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a primary registered office for a refrigerated logistics and cold storage warehousing entity. A physical Swiss registered office and operational facility (warehouse premises) are mandatory to obtain the required business license under cantonal commercial law and the Regulation on the Licensing of Warehousing and Logistics Activities. Virtual office can be used only as an auxiliary administrative service, provided the statutory registered office remains a physical address in the canton of registration and where the board meets with inspectable corporate records, in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 718 and Art. 650.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 65% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first operational year) due to mandatory cantonal licensing for pharmaceutical cold-chain storage under the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) and cantonal drug control authorities, and additional AML/CFT on-site verification by regulatory bodies if related-party transactions are involved.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations of 30 March 1911 (SR 220), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), in particular Arts. 621, 626, 629, 632, 640 and 707; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV; SR 221.411), Arts. 60-67; Company Names Ordinance (Art. 950 ff. OR).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons) for the canton in which the registered office is located, acting under the supervisory authority of the Federal Office of Justice (EJPD/FOJ). Statutory entry is administered on the official Swiss Commercial Register platform (zefix.ch / e-Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation and the Articles of Association (Gründungsurkunde und Statuten), notified to the Commercial Register via the official e-Register filing form R01, followed by publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital is CHF 100,000 fully subscribed (Art. 621 OR). At incorporation at least 20% of the nominal capital and not less than CHF 20,000 must be paid in cash; any issue premium (agio) must be paid in full. The paid-in funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account in the name of the company in formation with a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank, and the bank deposit certificate must be produced to the notary and the Commercial Register; funds are released only upon presentation of the final Commercial Register excerption (Handelsregisterauszug) confirming registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [NAME] AG. Adopted unanimously on [DATE] by written circular by the founding Board of Directors. 1. Capitalization. The share capital of CHF 100,000, fully subscribed per the Articles of Association, has been deposited in the blocked escrow account at [BANK] (ref. [NO.]) and shall remain restricted until Commercial Register registration is obtained. 2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [ADDRESS], [CANTON], Switzerland. 3. Appointments. The Board appoints [NAME A] as Chairperson, [NAME B] as Managing Director with individual signature authority, and [NAME C] as Director and Treasurer with individual signature authority. 4. Authorization. Management is directed to complete all Commercial Register filings and to appoint the statutory auditor. Resolved by unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Preliminary Corporate Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Central Business Name Registry (zefix.ch) administered by the Federal Commercial Register Authority; preliminary opinion of the cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the intended corporate name, including legal form suffix 'AG', in the central name index. Verify that the name is distinctive, truthful, not misleading, and does not conflict with protected marks or existing registrations in Switzerland. Submit an optional binding preliminary name inquiry (Vorabklärung) to the cantonal register office. If approved, provisionally reserve the name for a maximum of 60 days pending notarization.
required_dossiers: Completed official name reservation request form (e-Register preliminary notice)
Identification documents (passport / identity card) of all founders
zefix.ch name search proof printout
Declaration of non-conflicting trademarks or partnership agreement if any co-existing name is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of indistinguishability or confusion, file an amended preliminary request with a new name, or, if the decision is contested, lodge an administrative appeal to the cantonal appellate commission (Kantonale Rekurskommission / Handelsregister-Rekurs) within 30 days of the negative ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Escrow Account Opened with a FINMA-Regulated Swiss Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or Swiss PostFinance; bank confirmation subject to Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an escrow account in the name of the company in formation ('AG in Gründung') with the founding board members designated as authorized signatories. Deposit the full minimum capital of CHF 100,000, or the agreed multiple, by wire transfer from the subscribers' separate accounts. Request the bank's certificate of restriction (Sperrbestätigung / Form BCP), confirming that the funds are at the free disposal of the company only upon presentation of the Commercial Register registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of the draft Articles of Association issued by the notary public
Pay-in schedule identifying each subscriber and the amount contributed
Bank account opening and AML KYC forms
Source-of-funds documentation for each subscriber
Engagement letter authorizing the escrow arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML queries or declines the blocked account, respond with full source-of-wealth documentation, and, in case of continued refusal, substitute a different FINMA-regulated bank and provide a fresh escrow certificate before the notarial deed can be executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Deed of Incorporation and the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat du canton / Öffentliche Beurkundung) in the canton of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders and founding board members must appear in person before a Swiss notary public. The notary establishes the deed containing the company's name, registered office address, purpose (refrigerated logistics warehousing and warehousing of temperature-controlled pharmaceuticals), share capital, par value and classes of shares, board organization, auditing body, and publication provisions. The certificate of the blocked capital deposit is attached. The Articles of Association are read aloud and signed by all founders.
required_dossiers: Notarized draft deed of incorporation and Articles of Association (draft prepared by notary)
Bank blocked account certificate (Sperrbestätigung)
Identification documents of all founders
Subscription declarations signed by each shareholder
Board acceptance forms signed by the designated directors
Power of attorney, if any founder appears by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal deficiencies in the draft (e.g., faulty clauses on audit exemption or share transfer restrictions), the notary will return the draft for revision; the rectified document must be re-executed and signed afresh in the same notarial session or at the next available appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Submission to the Cantonal Commercial Register and Registration Proceedings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of incorporation; e-governance via the official Swiss e-Register platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified hard copy or digitally sealed notarial deed, the deposit-certified Articles of Association, the bank escrow confirmation, signed declaration of acceptance by each board member, and completed registration form R01 to the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office. The registrar verifies compliance with the Code of Obligations, checks the legal form and capital rules, and issues the extract and registration certificate upon approval.
required_dossiers: Database of executed notarial deed (original or certified copy)
Articles of Association certified copy
Bank blocked account certificate (original)
Board members' signed acceptance statements and specimen signatures (certified)
Statutory auditor's confirmation of acceptance, if an audit body is appointed
Completed registration form R01
Official fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query (salvatorische Anfechtung / Rueckfrage), cure the defect within 10 working days by submitting supplementary documentation. If registration is refused, the founders may appeal to the cantonal administrative court within 30 days of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Publication, UID Number Assignment and Release of Escrow Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB); Swiss Federal Statistical Office (for the business identification number UID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the commercial register entry, the SHAB publishes a legally required incorporation notice. The company automatically receives its permanent Swiss business identifier (UID / Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer). Thereafter present the official Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) to the bank, which releases the blocked capital to the company's unrestricted account. Apply for VAT registration if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000, and open statutory accounting records.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register certificate and full extract (dated)
UID confirmation letter
SHAB publication slip
Bank release-of-block instruction form signed by board
Evidence of registered office premises and lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or registry fails to release funds or the SHAB publication contains errors, request written formal correction from the Commercial Register Office (Berichtigung), and, in case of bank delay, provide a certified final extract and a board resolution on beneficiary allocation to compel execution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic, Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Schweizerisches Heilmittelinstitut) for pharmaceutical wholesale operations; the cantonal Department of Health and Labour (Amt für Gesundheit und Wirtschaft) for workplace and healthcare-related operations; the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) for environmental compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Wholesale Distribution Authorization for Medicinal Products (Bewilligung für den Grosshandel mit Arzneimitteln / Autorisation de grossiste), issued by Swissmedic under Art. 64 of the Therapeutic Products Act (TPA, SR 812.21), conditioned on demonstrated Good Distribution Practice (GDP) and a quality management system covering controlled-temperature storage.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) together with the cantonal environment office (Amt für Umwelt) of the canton of registered operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA screening registration only (Voruntersuchung / Screening) — a cold-storage warehouse for pharmaceuticals is normally below the category thresholds of the EIA Ordinance (SR 814.011), Annex 1. However, if the refrigeration system uses ammonia in a quantity exceeding 10 tonnes, the facility is classified as a Major Accident plant (Störfallverordnung / major-accident ordinance inspection) and requires a provisional major-accident risk review and safety report instead of a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Refrigerant leakage must comply with the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (SR 814.81): annual leak checks and repair within 30 days for installations containing >= 10 kg of fluorinated greenhouse gases; no HFC/HFO discharge above 200 g per tonne of cooling capacity without immediate repair records. Wastewater and cooling-tower blowdown must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (SR 814.201), including maximum discharge temperature of 30 °C, pH 6.5-9.5, and zero discharge of chromium, ammonia, or biocides above the micro-pollutant legal limits. Condensate and washing water from hygiene cleaning operations of the cold-storage areas must be directed to the municipal sewer system under a discharge consent with a daily organic load analysis if connected to industrial lines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal Fire Police (Feuerpolizei) fire-safety certificate confirming compliance with VKF / AEAI fire-protection directives, including fire compartmentalization, sprinkler or gas suppression design for the pharmaceutical high-bay frozen areas, and evacuation signage. Structural load inspection and static certificate issued by the building inspectorate for the high-rack refrigerated warehouse, verifying pallet-rack seismic load and stored-floor load capacity. Workplace clearance from SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) and the cantonal labour inspectorate confirming safe entry / exit for sub-zero personnel zones, thermal work-rule conformity (EN ISO / temperature-workplace ordinance), emergency rescue plan for locked cold-storage cells, and the required safety officers' signage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC) in Bern; official VAT and customs portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT e-filing via ESTV e-services platform (Mein ESTV / AFC en ligne).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign corporations performing taxable supplies in Switzerland, including cold-storage warehousing at Swiss premises, must register for Swiss VAT before commencing activity. A non-established entity must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (Art. 73 VAT Act) and file the registration application (official form or ESTV e-services) indicating expected Swiss turnover and foreign tax identifier; the ESTV then issues the Swiss business identifier (UID) and the VAT number (MWST-Nr / Numéro TVA). Registration is mandatory where net taxable Swiss turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per calendar year (Art. 10 VAT Act). A Swiss-resident Aktiengesellschaft is automatically enrolled via the commercial registry and receives the UID, which serves as the statutory tax identification number for corporate and VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Swiss AG is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to federal corporate income tax (8.5% statutory on profit after federal tax; aggregate federal-cantonal effective rate typically 11-21% depending on canton) plus cantonal/communal profit tax and capital tax at its registered seat (e.g. Zug or Zurich). The AG is taxed at entity level with no pass-through eligibility. Foreign income of a resident AG is generally subject to Swiss taxation on worldwide income, with relief granted for foreign permanent establishments under double taxation treaties and cantonal application of the territorial exemption method.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide US-style check-the-box elections. Available mechanisms include: (i) Swiss group taxation / fiscal unity election for profit and capital taxes under Art. 9 Tax Harmonisation Act, generally available for qualifying 100% group structures from tax year 2025/2026; (ii) participation relief election exempting qualifying income and capital gains from substantial shareholdings (Art. 69 DBG); (iii) deemed liquidation / step-up election upon cross-border migration; (iv) VAT option to tax otherwise exempt supplies such as real property and certain financial services (Arts. 21-22 VAT Act); and (v) hybrid mismatch rules implementing OECD BEPS Action 2, which operate as mandatory disallowances rather than elective mechanisms for the AG and its foreign related parties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto), administered by the ESTV/AFC; customs duties are administered separately by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG/FOCBS).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual net taxable turnover from supplies in Switzerland (Art. 10 VAT Act). Cold-storage warehousing is a service supplied where the goods are physically located (Art. 8 VAT Act), so a Swiss AG operating cold-chain facilities always has a Swiss VAT nexus. Voluntary registration is allowed below CHF 100,000 where the operator supplies taxable services. Non-established foreign suppliers of electronically supplied services face mandatory registration from the first franc in certain consumer B2C scenarios under ESTV administrative practice.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority API clearance, or digital stamping regime. Since 30 June 2020, the QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is the mandatory payment-slip format in Swiss payment processing. B2B e-invoicing follows Swiss implementation guidelines (eBill, eCH-0113 XML/UBL) but remains voluntary; paper invoices are lawful. All invoices, including zero-rated export invoices, must satisfy the statutory content requirements of Art. 81 VAT Act (supplier name and address, UID/MWST number, date, description of supply, consideration, and VAT rate including 0%) and must be retained for ten years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% with full input VAT deduction applies to: (1) exports of goods where the seller physically transports the goods out of Swiss customs territory and holds valid customs export proof (e-dec / Ausfuhrschein); (2) services directly and specifically connected to the export or import of goods (Art. 23(2)(c) VAT Act), including transport, handling, freight, and for a cold-chain operator, warehousing/storage services rendered in Switzerland for goods destined for export to an overseas principal, provided the direct link to the export transaction is documented; (3) services performed on movable goods (such as repackaging or temperature monitoring) for a foreign customer where the goods are thereafter exported from Switzerland (Art. 23(3) VAT Act); and (4) supplies into customs warehousing under duty suspension (Zolllager). Purely domestic storage for a Swiss-based customer remains taxable at 8.1% at the place of performance. Export must occur through Swiss customs territory, transport documents must evidence exit abroad, and the supplier must retain all proof for a minimum of ten years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (e-dec) with exit confirmation and unique customs transaction reference (CRC / Ausfuhrschein)
Commercial invoice and export packing list with Incoterms 2020 terms and legal exporter entity names
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, CMR consignment note, or air waybill (AWB) evidencing physical exit from Swiss customs territory
Customs transit document (T1/T2) or Swiss customs warehouse withdrawal form where goods move through bonded logistics
Foreign destination customs import declaration of the buyer jurisdiction (where available)
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank SWIFT MT103, or bank statement evidencing actual receipt of foreign currency consideration from the overseas customer
Signed warehouse custody and temperature-monitoring records linking the exported pharmaceutical lot to the storage services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT is self-assessed and the ESTV may audit retrospectively for up to five years, with a ten-year period in cases of fraud. Where zero-rating is claimed without substantiated customs or remittance evidence, the tax authority retroactively recharacterises the supply as taxable at 8.1%, issues a tax reassessment (Nachbelastung) with arrears interest (approximately 4.5-5% per annum), and may impose administrative penalties under Arts. 84-86 VAT Act: intentional tax evasion carries a fine of up to four times the evaded tax and criminal prosecution of responsible officers; negligence and record-keeping violations carry fines of up to CHF 8,000 per breach. Export proof must be credible and complete generally within 180 days of invoicing or foreign-currency remittance; missing or fraudulent FX repatriation evidence can trigger full clawback, denial of input VAT recovery, and interest. Repeated qualified VAT fraud is prosecuted under the Swiss Criminal Code and may result in imprisonment; the burden of proving eligibility for zero-rating rests entirely on the taxable person.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible under a free-float regime. Switzerland imposes no exchange control restrictions on current or capital account transactions, including capital injections, trade settlements, or dividend repatriation. Capital imports and exports are unrestricted and require only statistical reporting for balance-of-payments purposes. Profit remittance is subject to the Swiss dividend withholding tax of 35% at source, with full or partial refund available under domestic participation relief or an applicable double taxation treaty, provided the beneficial owner supplies the requisite Swiss Form 82 / R-request and proof of tax residence. There are no prior-authorization requirements, surrender obligations, or conversion queues for corporate treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland does not impose statutory surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or fixed repatriation timelines for export receipts. A Swiss AG engaged in refrigerated logistics may retain export proceeds in foreign currency indefinitely. Export invoices must be settled through the corporate operational account, and individual transactions above CHF 5 million or unusual cross-border flows may be subject to the SNB's mandatory balance-of-payments reporting thresholds. No foreign-exchange approval is required; the sole obligations are accurate accounting and compliance with the Swiss Federal Act on Monetary and Payment Instruments and the SNB's statistical reporting directives for BoP and international investment position surveys.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) are of Medium feasibility for this treasury blueprint. A foreign EMI domiciled in the EU/EEA or UK cannot passport its e-money licence into Switzerland; nor does a Crypto Valley-based fintech licence authorise commercial deposit-taking beyond the CHF 100 million threshold without full banking authorisation. Consequently, an offshore EMI may serve only as a low-balance collection corridor or payment initiation layer, with settlement ultimately routed through a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or a Swiss fintech bank holding a banking licence under Article 1b of the Swiss Banking Act. Pure foreign EMI accounts are not suitable for the capital escrow, customs-shielded liquidity reserves, or ISIC 5210 trade disbursement functions. A Swiss-registered, FINMA-licensed financial technology company (e.g., an entity holding a fintech banking licence) is the only viable direct EMI route, and it must be fully integrated into the group's KYC/AML framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money-laundering legislation (AMLA / FINMA Circular 2024/1) permits remote onboarding through an audited video-identification process, provided the verification is performed by a recognised Swiss-based professional and the client files meet the standard of 'comparable reliability'. However, for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of a newly incorporated AG, most Tier-1 Swiss banks require at least one physical meeting with the board delegate and the signatory treasurer at a Swiss branch, or an in-person appearance before a Swiss notary for the capital-escrow mandate and the certified signature card. Where the entire board is non-resident, banks typically impose enhanced due diligence: documentary certification by a Swiss notary, apostilled corporate extracts, and bank-to-bank reference from the home-country institution. Pure remote onboarding without any in-country footprint is possible only for low-risk domiciled companies with all Swiss-resident directors; this entity structure is therefore expected to follow the hybrid route: a remote video KYC plus one physical signatory appearance at the primary bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material discrepancy between the declared corporate purpose (ISIC 5210 cold storage warehousing) and high-volume capital inflow through the escrow account during the pre-revenue phase
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised board resolution confirming the capital increase and escrow purpose; audited 24-month business plan; executed warehouse leases or letters of intent from pharmaceutical shippers; pro-forma invoices for refrigeration equipment and facility fit-out; expected transaction-volume forecast; bank references from the shareholder's home institution; confirmation that no third-party pass-through lending is contemplated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Origin of subscribed capital or share-premium payments routed through a jurisdiction with opaque corporate registries or a low effective tax rate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of asset provenance from the remitting bank; complete source-of-wealth statements; audited financial statements of the investing shareholder; corporate registry excerpt and UBO attestation of the investing entity; tax residence certificate; explanation of the commercial rationale for routing; commitment to provide quarterly source-of-funds updates during the first 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or multi-layered ownership chain with bearer-share legacy or opaque nominees at the ultimate holding level
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current excerpt from the Swiss Commercial Register confirming registered share structure (no bearer shares); full organisational chart from beneficial owner to the AG; Swiss UBO register declaration (Annex to the Articles of Association); nominee-shareholder waiver or direct bank confirmation of natural-person UBO; statutory declaration of no sanctioned parties or politically exposed persons (PEPs) within the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list hit or adverse negative news on a UBO, finance director, or counterparty bank of the group
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions-screening report from a recognised provider; negative-news search across global sanctions regimes (UN, EU, UK, OFAC, SECO); open-source intelligence summary; sworn declaration and written explanation from the affected person; remedial remediation letter; confirmation that the group will undertake monthly re-screening and will notify the account-holding bank immediately upon any change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in the operational purpose of holding both a capital escrow account and multiple operational sub-accounts in different currencies, raising structuring or layering concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group treasury policy (ALM and FX risk charter); schedule of expected currency netting and clearing flows; customer contracts linking payment rails (ACH_Direct and Bank_Wire) to specific operational accounts; capital-control and segregation matrix; cash-flow forecast by currency showing the liquidity need for CHF, EUR, and USD positions; audit committee minutes approving the account structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for the CHF capital injection relies on the SIC/eSIC system for domestic transfers or a SWIFT MT103 for international wire arrivals. The shareholder must remit from its own account in its home jurisdiction to the beneficiary account at the Swiss Tier-1 bank, referencing the Swiss notarial deed date and the purpose code for capital contribution (OECD's capital-liability classification, typically category 3B12 or the SNB's statistical code for 'Beteiligungskapital' / direct investment equity). The bank will verify that the beneficiary account reflects the exact corporate name, that the remitter is the registered shareholder, and that no deferred-payment or loan structure is concealed. The bank must receive the notarised minutes of the capital increase and the confirmation of the bank's own account-opening documentation before accepting post-incorporation contributions. The SNB requires the receiving bank to report the transaction for balance-of-payments statistics; no exchange-control approval is needed. Funds arriving in foreign currency may be converted into CHF at the client's discretion or held in a corresponding nostro-based foreign-currency sub-account; the credit must not be split into artificial tranches below CHF 10,000 to avoid structuring suspicion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the cold-storage and refrigerated logistics operations must be cleared via (i) SWIFT MT103 for all cross-border vendor, energy-trading and tolling payments denominated in foreign currency; (ii) the SIC system for domestic CHF obligations; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated EU counterparties; and (iv) a documentary collection or irrevocable commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) for large refrigerated pharmaceutical shipments requiring the presentation of temperature-log evidence, customs documents, and insurance certificates. ACH_Direct is acceptable only for recurring low-value domestic-esque USD flows processed through the Swiss bank's US clearing partner, not for primary trade settlements. All beneficiary names must exactly match KYC records; invoices must be retained to substantiate the commercial underlying of the transfer; transactions exceeding CHF 50,000 must be encoded with the correct payment purpose description (e.g., 'payment for storage and handling services under ISIC 5210'); and the bank's statutory reporting must be discharged without delays. For open-account trade credit, intercompany settlement should be netted under an approved cash-pooling agreement and supported by arm's-length transfer pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla OTC foreign-exchange forwards (CHF/EUR, CHF/USD, EUR/USD) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a Swiss bank's master FX agreement, with margining or netting as agreed

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to currencies without deliverable onshore forward markets (e.g., CNY, INR, or certain emerging-market currencies of pharmaceutical-source counterparties), settled in CHF or USD and subject to the bank's internal restrictions
Short-dated FX swaps to cover temporary liquidity mismatches between CHF receipts and foreign-currency disbursements without altering the economic open position beyond the swap maturity

Cross-currency basis swaps for long-term structural hedges of the capital escrow and intercompany funding positions where a foreign shareholder provides subordinated shareholder loans in another currency

FX options (European-style) for the cap-and-floor protection of the quarterly energy-cost and temperature-controlled fuel hedges, when approved by the board treasury committee and subject to the investment policy statement
Outright spot transactions executed via the SIC/SWIFT settlement system, which constitute the default clearing hedge for transaction-driven exposures rather than speculative open positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Annual General Meeting and adoption of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting (corporate action recorded in minutes; no regulatory filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance-sheet date (Art. 699 para. 3 CO); calendar-year companies no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directorial liability for losses; shareholder may petition the court to convene the meeting; no automatic administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income and capital tax return (federal and cantonal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax authority at the registered office (ESTV for federal elements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Canton-specific; commonly within 3–5 months of year-end; extensions available; calendar-year companies usually required by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest (statutory rates), default assessment, procedural fines, debt enforcement and possible compulsory liquidation in cases of persistent non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, semi-annual or quarterly depending on turnover; return and payment due generally within 60 days after the end of the relevant VAT period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum, administrative fines under the Swiss VAT Act, and recovery procedures through statutory debt enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding tax declaration and payment (Verrechnungssteuer) if dividends, interest or similar taxable payments are made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Withholding Tax section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the statutory period following taxable payment; periodic return and payment schedule as prescribed by ESTV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at statutory rates, administrative fines, and obligation to retroactively remit under-withheld tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Old-age and survivors insurance (AHV) wage statement and social security contributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal social security compensation office (AHV/IV/EO) and supplementary institutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly contribution settlements as required; annual wage statement due by end of January following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid contributions, fines for declaration violations, and execution proceedings for collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory for an AG that is a public company or exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, 250 full-time employees. Other AGs require a limited statutory audit unless a valid unanimous shareholder opt-out applies and the company has no more than 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting rules; Swiss GAAP FER accepted as good practice; IFRS permitted and commonly used for listed and consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO confirmation is filed in Switzerland. The AG must keep its share register current and, only if bearer shares or participation certificates exist, maintain a register of beneficial owners (Art. 697j CO). At each annual general meeting, the board reviews and confirms the completeness of corporate registers in the minutes; authorities may request registers for inspection and may impose administrative fines for incomplete records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800–2,500 per annum depending on canton and agent service level
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–15,000 for ordinary audit; USD 1,500–4,500 for limited audit; nil if valid opt-out applies
